plan: To preserve capital, we'll exit all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and other leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU).
This reduces overall portfolio risk and cures the leveraged ETF mandate breach.
We will also trim QQQI to 20% to cap single-name exposure and increase our cash buffer.
This strategy prioritizes stability and low drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation, targeting around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged exposure and increasing cash, leading to lower expected drawdowns.

plan: For a balanced approach, we'll trim SOXL and SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure and cure the mandate breach.
Other leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU) will also be trimmed to reduce overall concentration.
We will add NET, a high-quality scanner setup, to diversify and add growth potential.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan focuses on risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a strong new setup, aiming for moderate growth with controlled drawdowns.

plan: For aggressive growth, we will increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and other leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU).
This strategy leans into higher-beta assets to amplify potential returns.
We will also buy NET, a top-scoring scanner setup, to further concentrate in strong opportunities.
This approach uses leverage to stretch growth, accepting higher risk and wider stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets around 4% per month by stretching into leveraged ETFs and concentrating in high-scoring setups. Be aware this significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay/rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the higher risk.

plan: To prioritize income, we will sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU).
This significantly reduces volatility and risk, aligning with an income-focused strategy.
We will add to QQQI, an income/covered-call ETF, to increase steady monthly distributions.
This plan aims for low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month by rotating into income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable distributions, but remember distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
